deviation.decided_by: lane-2 during TF-0142 D4 gate adjudication; classified under §R5 scope-2 as backlog-P1, not escalated to P0
deviation.impact: Judged backlog-P1, NOT fixed this round. Rationale: all 25 known mismatches are provably non-round-caused (round-diff 590588791..HEAD intersected with the 25 subject files is empty), and TF-0142's non_goals explicitly forbid recomputing maturity hashes; running scripts 5-6 to closure is system-maturity backlog work outside scope-1. Mitigation landed instead of a fix: the blind spot is written into GATE-BASELINE.md §4.1 and DEV-PROTOCOL §D4.3 as a named known-unknown, and the tightened L2 criterion requires running `maturity:residual` and `maturity:traceability` SEPARATELY (not via the chain) so the blind spot cannot silently persist into milestone acceptance. maturity:validate does not enter L1 at all, so this does not gate any per-task closeout. Whoever later owns the maturity backlog must clear scripts 5-6 before the 25-item baseline can be called complete.
deviation.summary: pnpm maturity:validate is a 6-script && chain: audit-baseline-check -> validate-system-maturity-plan -> validate-test-gates -> validate-system-maturity-evidence -> run-system-maturity-residual-audit -> validate-system-maturity-traceability. It exits 1 at script 4 (validate-system-maturity-evidence, FAILED (25)), so scripts 5 and 6 NEVER RUN. Their state is UNKNOWN, not green. Any statement of the form 'maturity has 25 problems' is therefore incomplete: the true count is 25 plus whatever scripts 5-6 would report. This blind spot was not previously recorded anywhere; TF-0142's evidence and the round's planning docs both cite only the 25 mismatches.

rationale: TF-0142 classified all 25 maturity:validate A2 hash mismatches as backlog-debt (mechanically proven non-round-caused). While doing so it surfaced a distinct, previously unrecorded problem that is NOT one of the 25: the maturity:validate && chain short-circuits at script 4 of 6, so scripts 5 and 6 never execute and their pass/fail state is UNKNOWN rather than green. Per §R5 scope-2 this is a newly discovered problem being judged 'not fixed this round', which is exactly §R4 deviation trigger (c) and therefore must be recorded rather than only footnoted in a doc.
